text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prime Minister Goran Persson in centre of political storm of protest about his comments on China's political stability. The Liberal party is seeking a vote of no confidence in him in parliament.

- Professor Lars Calmfors and his commission set up to investigate a possible Swedish link to Europe's currency union do not believe the Swedish government can fulfil its target of cutting unemployment in half by 2000.
This was one reason why the committee in a report said Sweden should not join the EMU when it starts in 1999 but leave the question of participation open.

- Swedish drugs group Astra posts an eight percent higher pre-tax profit of almost 10 billion crowns despite the impact of a stronger crown. Sales of its key drug Losec, the ulcer treatment agent, continued to show strong growth.
- U.S. company Hemasure sues Pharmacia & Upjohn for 1.8 billion crowns for allegedly breaking a contract for the planned sale of products from Pharmacia's blood plasma division.
- Prime Minister Goran Persson's comments during a visit to China about the country's political stability have prompted opposition parties to call for a vote of no confidence in his leadership.

- The Calmfors commission report says Sweden should join Europe's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), but not when it starts in 1999. It said Swden's high unemployment, currently running at over 12 percent in total, must first go down.

- Electricity prices have fallen in both Sweden and Norway following a mild autumn, impacting electricity companies. The average price has dropped to 0.21 Norwegian crowns per kilowatt hour from 0.26 crowns. But the movement of prices later in the year is unclear.

- Sweden's state-owned AMU group, the largest vocational training company in Sweden, has started in internal audit, The company is in economic crisis and may suffer a loss of one billion crowns this year.

- The merger of British Telecom with MCi Communications will have positive consequences for Stockholm-based Telenordia which is part-owned by BT. Telenordia president Daniel Johansson said its global services, sold under the name Concert, could be provided more simply.
- A government report, called the Calmfors Report, on the effects of Swedish participation in Europe's single currency recommends Sweden not join the EMU at its scheduled 1999 start.
